channel.title: FontLab Blog
channel.description: News, technical writing, and updates from FontLab.

item.title: FontLab VI 6.1.4: open and export .glyphs files
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI 6.1.4 adds high-precision segment editing, a snapping Knife, smarter glyph deletion — and, the headline, the ability to open and export .glyphs files on both Mac and Windows.

item.title: Mac updates for FontLab Studio, TypeTool and Fontographer
item.author: FontLab
item.description: We have released Mac updates for FontLab Studio 5 (5.1.6), TypeTool (3.1.3) and Fontographer (5.2.4), fixing font open/export and copy-paste problems on recent macOS releases.

item.title: FontLab VI 6.1.3: faster, more precise, more streamlined
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI 6.1.3 is faster and leaner — up to 2× quicker to open and save, using up to 40% less memory — with sharper editing, better class and feature handling, and Sketchboard text frames.

item.title: FontLab VI 6.1.2: printing, Echo Text and the Tables panel
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI 6.1.2 adds printing, synchronized text across windows, a Tables panel for custom OpenType tables, and a faster Classes panel.

item.title: Font filters, components and glyph metrics in FontLab VI 6.1
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI 6.1 adds three things type designers had been asking for: real, standards-compliant components, a Font window sidebar that filters glyphs by script and category, and metrics expressions that link spacing across glyphs, layers and masters.

item.title: Free FontLab VI workshops at ATypI Antwerp
item.author: FontLab
item.description: In September 2018, FontLab ran three free FontLab VI workshops at the ATypI Antwerp conference — two introductory sessions in the morning and an advanced one in the afternoon.

item.title: FontLab VI 6.0.9 update
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI 6.0.9, together with the previous 6.0.8 update, brought a batch of editing and export improvements. Both were free updates.

item.title: FontLab Studio, TypeTool & old TransType on macOS 10.13 High Sierra
item.author: FontLab
item.description: A compatibility note for owners of the older apps: FontLab Studio 5, TypeTool 3, and TransType Pro 3 had real problems on macOS 10.13 “High Sierra” and 10.14 “Mojave.” Here is what broke and what to do about it.

item.title: What's up with VI @ FontLab?
item.author: FontLab
item.description: A quick status report from the Public Preview period: FontLab VI was close to done, the bug list was short, and Variable Fonts were the last big feature going in.

item.title: FontLab VI on macOS 10.9
item.author: FontLab
item.description: Newer FontLab VI builds require macOS 10.10 Yosemite or later. Earlier Public Preview builds ran on 10.9 Mavericks; that support is ending.

item.title: Deprecated vs. discontinued
item.author: FontLab
item.description: “Discontinued” and “deprecated” sound like the same thing. At FontLab they mean two different fates for an old product, and the difference matters if you depend on one of them.

item.title: FontLab VI ship update
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI will not ship in 2016 after all. The new target is February.

item.title: Free FontLab VI Public Preview for Windows
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI Public Preview is now available for Windows, alongside an updated Mac build. It is free until the final app ships.

item.title: FontLab's plans for OpenType 1.8 variable fonts
item.author: FontLab
item.description: At the ATypI conference in Warsaw, Google, Microsoft, Apple, and Adobe jointly unveiled version 1.8 of the OpenType specification — and with it, variable fonts.

item.title: New FontLab VI Public Preview for Mac
item.author: FontLab
item.description: A new FontLab VI Public Preview for Mac is out, adding context menus, a Gallery panel for named shapes, faster glyph access, and italic-angle drawing.

item.title: FontLab VI Public Preview 2 for Mac
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab VI Public Preview 2 (build 5844) is out for Mac, following the expiry of the first preview. We are still not calling it a beta.

item.title: All FontLab products run on macOS 10.9 Mavericks
item.author: FontLab
item.description: FontLab tested its current product line against macOS 10.9 Mavericks. Everything passed.

item.title: OpenType Layout feature classification
item.author: FontLab
item.description: OpenType Layout features drive the correct display of complex scripts like Arabic and Indic, and they let users apply advanced typographic formatting. This is a classification of the registered feature tags, written for developers building UI to expose them.

item.title: On fractional coordinates
item.author: FontLab
item.description: Round a number too early and the error never leaves. That is the whole case for working in fractional coordinates while you design, and rounding to a grid only when you ship.

item.title: Five centuries of line — Dürer, Hogarth, Bewick, Doré
item.author: Vexy Lines
item.description:
{.illu-thumb }

A line can carry tone, texture, shadow, and emotion — and never once pretend to be a photograph. That is the whole argument of five centuries of printmaking, made with a burin, a graver, and eventually a stylus.

item.title: Calfonts: italics that aren’t just slanted romans
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Italics are the part of a font family that most often gets shipped wrong — slanted romans, no cursive structure, lopsided ovals. The Calfonts italic tutorial walks through what it actually takes to draw an italic that earns its place next to the roman.

item.title: Briem: how to draw an italic (and why the slanted-roman trap is real)
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Italic is not roman tilted to the right. Slant your upright a and what you get is a tilted a, not an italic a — the structure is wrong, the rhythm is wrong, the connection points are wrong.

item.title: Color fonts: the next big thing? A FontLab tutorial
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Back in 2014, color fonts were a brand new frontier. This 103-minute tutorial with Adam Twardoch was one of the first deep dives into how to actually make them.

item.title: Basics of Python scripting in FontLab Studio 5
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Automation unlocks the real power of a professional font editor. In this 70-minute tutorial, Adam Twardoch introduces Python scripting inside FontLab Studio 5.

item.title: How to space a font
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Spacing is where type design lives or dies. In this 53-minute tutorial, Thomas Phinney walks through sidebearings, optical principles, and the practical workflow inside FontLab Studio 5.

item.title: FontLab VI 6.1: components, sidebar filters, and metrics expressions
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

FontLab VI 6.1 arrived in October 2018. It added standards-compliant components, a Font window sidebar for glyph filtering, and linked metrics expressions.

item.title: Introducing FontLab 7: the pro font editor, evolved
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

FontLab 7 is a major upgrade to FontLab VI, arriving after a summer and autumn of concentrated work, with more than 250 new features, fixes, and improvements.

item.title: Bézier and de Casteljau: two engineers, one beautiful curve
item.author: FontLab
item.description:
{.illu-thumb }

In 1958, Paul de Casteljau at Citroën worked out the mathematics of the curves we now draw with every day. A few years later Pierre Bézier at Renault arrived at the same idea independently and published it in 1962.

item.title: FontLab Studio 5 and the Fontographer acquisition
item.author: FontLab
Fontographer
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

2005 was a pivotal year for Fontlab Ltd. The company shipped FontLab Studio 5, which became the dominant professional font editor for the next decade. FontLab also acquired Fontographer from Macromedia, reviving a tool that had been dormant since the mid-1990s.

item.title: TransType 4 for Mac and Windows
item.author: TransType
item.description:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

TransType 4 arrived in December 2013 as a complete rewrite of our font conversion app. It added multi-color OpenType output and web font export to its core toolkit.
